anchors.name: BCBS principles for operational resilience
anchors.binding: Principles for banks from the Basel Committee, final and marked current.
anchors.asks: Banks should be able to withstand operational disruption, including technology failures, across their critical operations and the third parties that support them.
anchors.evidence: A test set and replay script your second line can re-run whenever a vendor's model may have changed, with every failure listed.

anchors.name: BCBS principles for third-party risk
anchors.binding: Principles for the sound management of third-party risk, for banks; final and marked current.
anchors.asks: A life-cycle approach to third-party arrangements: due diligence before a bank relies on a provider, and monitoring while it does. The principles cover a broader range of arrangements than traditional outsourcing, so an AI vendor's service can fall within them.
anchors.evidence: A pre-contract evaluation of the vendor's AI on your own cases, and a re-test report each time its model may have changed.

anchors.name: DORA: duties of EU financial entities
anchors.binding: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, applied from 17 January 2025 to banks, insurers and other financial entities in the EU.
anchors.asks: In the EU, DORA requires banks, insurers and other financial entities to keep a register of their ICT arrangements and to put set terms into those contracts. It also asks them to manage ICT risk and ICT third-party risk, and to test their digital operational resilience. AI services that EU financial entities buy are ICT services.
anchors.evidence: Vendor AI test reports and model-change records your team can keep with its register of ICT arrangements.

anchors.name: FSB report on monitoring AI adoption in the financial sector
anchors.binding: A non-binding report to financial authorities.
anchors.asks: Flags third-party dependency and service-provider concentration in the generative AI supply chain, model risk and governance weaknesses, and asks authorities to monitor them.
anchors.evidence: Evaluation reports that record the vendor, model and version tested.

anchors.name: IOSCO supervisory toolkit for AI in capital markets
anchors.binding: Non-binding, and applicable across regulatory models.
anchors.asks: Four supervisory focus areas: governance and risk management; third-party and outsourcing risk; disclosure; and recordkeeping and reporting. It covers machine learning and generative AI across the life cycle.
anchors.evidence: Test records and a model-change log kept with each evaluation.

anchors.name: EU AI Act Annex III 5(b) and 5(c)
anchors.binding: Law in the EU: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
anchors.asks: Credit scoring and creditworthiness assessment of individuals (fraud detection excluded), and risk assessment and pricing for life and health insurance, are high-risk uses from 2 December 2027 (as amended in July 2026). Their deployers must assess the impact on fundamental rights before first use (Art 27).
anchors.evidence: Measured test results and a failure list for the scoring or pricing system, which your team can draw on for its impact assessment.
